nodes.label: Spree::SingleStoreResource concern adoption
nodes.author: Damian (getvendo)
nodes.rationale: Replaces StoreScopedResource's many-to-many joins(:stores) with FK-based for_store + ensure_store + immutability, mirroring the Product single-owner migration.

nodes.label: LegacyMultiStoreSupport deprecation bridge
nodes.author: Damian (getvendo)
nodes.rationale: stores/store_ids accessors preserved as deprecation bridges returning Array(store); real multi-store sharing moves to the spree_multi_store extension overlaying the untouched join tables.

nodes.label: backorder_limit universal oversell cap
nodes.author: Damian (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: One integer bounds overselling for both backorder and pre-order (empty = unlimited); pre-order is backorder-with-a-delivery-promise so the two share one cap, enforced solely in Quantifier#can_supply?.

nodes.label: Pre-order as out-of-stock selling behavior, not publishing concept
nodes.author: Damian (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: An earlier draft gated pre-order on a future published_at, excluding the common live-restock case; decoupling pre-order from publishing fixes both concerns — visibility and out-of-stock behavior are independent switches.
nodes.norm_label: pre-order as out-of-stock selling behavior, not publishing concept

nodes.label: Spree::OrderApproval model
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Merchant-side (store owner) order approval; single-level in 5.5, multi-level (manager/finance/admin) in 6.0. Distinct from B2B buyer-org cart-side approvals deferred to 6.0.

nodes.label: Spree::OrderCancellation model
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Replaces denormalized canceled_at/canceler_id columns with an append-only history model capturing reason, restock, and refund coupling; 5.5 keeps denormalized columns mirroring the latest record, 6.0 drops them.

nodes.label: OptionValue color_code + image
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Closes gap vs Shopify ProductOptionValueSwatch and Saleor AttributeValue by adding visual metadata to option values.

nodes.label: OptionType kind rendering hint
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Adds dropdown/color_swatch/buttons rendering hint so frontends don't need to hardcode option type name checks like the deprecated color? method.

nodes.label: Spree::SearchProvider::Base
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Pluggable search+filter+facet contract so AR keeps security/visibility while the provider owns search, filtering and aggregation.

nodes.label: MetafieldDefinition.filterable facets
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Extends faceted filtering beyond OptionType to structured metafield attributes (material, brand, weight class).

nodes.label: PgSearch removal
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: PgSearch is PostgreSQL-only and creates dual code paths for marginal benefit over ILIKE; Meilisearch is the recommended upgrade instead.

nodes.label: Spree::CustomField constant alias (5.5 shim)
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: module Spree; CustomField = Metafield; end lets controllers/extensions reference the 6.0-bound name today without subclassing, which would fight STI.

nodes.label: custom_fieldable route concern
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Mounts nested custom_fields resources under each custom-fieldable parent, keeping URLs human-readable versus a polymorphic flat endpoint.

nodes.label: Spree::DisplayOn concern (frozen, dropped in 6.0)
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: front_end-only tri-state doesn't map to a real workflow since admin staff need visibility into every payment/shipping option; collapses to a boolean storefront_visible mirroring the custom-fields plan.

nodes.label: Custom Fields vs Metadata two-system design
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Metadata is private developer-owned schemaless JSON (never exposed to customers); Custom Fields are public, typed, merchant-managed structured data — razor-sharp boundary avoiding the Shopify metafield naming confusion.
nodes.norm_label: custom fields vs metadata two-system design

nodes.label: field_type token vocabulary
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Exposes abstract tokens (short_text, number, etc.) instead of leaking Ruby STI class names across the API, matching Shopify/Saleor/Vendure/commercetools convention.

nodes.label: POST /translations/batch single write surface
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: One atomic batch endpoint (not embedded writes, not per-resource endpoints) so a multi-entity dual-save (option type + values) is transactional; reads stay a separate read-only per-resource matrix.

nodes.label: TranslatableResource#upsert_translations
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Write mechanics live on the model concern itself rather than a service, avoiding DI ceremony; omit-to-leave-alone, empty-string clears, null deletes a cell.

nodes.label: Server-side advisory staleness (source_digest)
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Takes Shopify's staleness idea but drops the mandatory digest requirement on write since client-side digest computation is unreproducible across sanitizers.

nodes.label: spree eject CLI command
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Lets a generated project switch from prebuilt Docker image to local backend/ builds for customization.

nodes.label: spree/spree-starter template repo
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth Rails app for users, core devs, CI, and Docker releases, replacing the non-portable monorepo server/ directory.

nodes.label: normalizeMoneyInput dashboard util
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Parses merchant's locale-formatted input into canonical form in the browser using Intl.NumberFormat.formatToParts before it reaches the API.

nodes.label: API-surface-now, model-rename-later bridge pattern
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Change API surface (serializers, response keys, endpoint paths) in 5.4 while models stay unchanged until 6.0, giving storefront devs the final API shape early with clean, alias-free breaks.

nodes.label: Canonical decimal string money contract
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.rationale: Industry standard (Shopify, Saleor, Vendure, Medusa) treats money API format as canonical/locale-agnostic; localized parsing happens client-side, replacing the non-standard x-spree-locale-driven server parse.

nodes.label: Merchandising media scope boundary (not a DAM)
nodes.author: Damian + Claude
nodes.norm_label: merchandising media scope boundary (not a dam)

nodes.label: spree-expert subagent
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.rationale: Subagent for multi-step investigations, shipped alongside 25 skills, 2 slash commands, and 2 safety hooks (block destructive db, warn on hardcoded secrets).

nodes.label: spree api — Admin API command group in @spree/cli
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.norm_label: spree api — admin api command group in @spree/cli

nodes.label: CLI-first sequencing decision
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.rationale: Developer agents already have shell access needing zero client config; consumer MCP clients are blocked on OAuth 2.1 work; CLI is immune to MCP protocol churn. Mirrors Shopify's AI Toolkit CLI approach (no official Admin MCP).

nodes.label: Generic verbs, not per-resource subcommands
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.rationale: spree api get /products, never spree products list — precedent is gh api; a per-resource family across ~38 resources would duplicate @spree/admin-sdk and add nothing for agents.

nodes.label: npx skills add distribution channel
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.rationale: Tool-agnostic distribution via vercel-labs/skills CLI, same channel adopted by Medusa, shadcn/ui, Anthropic, Vercel; supports 70+ agentic CLIs with each tool's native file convention.

nodes.label: HttpOnly refresh cookie, in-memory access token
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.rationale: Moves refresh token out of localStorage (readable by any JS) into HttpOnly cookie scoped to /auth; follows Saleor's storefront Auth SDK pattern.
nodes.norm_label: httponly refresh cookie, in-memory access token

nodes.label: No separate CSRF token decision
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.rationale: SameSite cookie attributes + CORS AllowedOrigin allowlist already block cross-site attachment/preflight; a double-submit token would only help if AllowedOrigin were misconfigured to '*', a deeper problem anyway.

nodes.label: useExport hook (create + poll + download)
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.rationale: Wraps SDK create with 2s polling up to 5 minutes, then triggers browser download; falls back to 'check your email' toast on timeout, backed by the existing ExportMailer.

nodes.label: Signed Blob URL download (not server redirect)
nodes.author: Damian Legawiec
nodes.rationale: An SPA on a different origin can't reliably download an attachment through a server-side redirect while keeping JWT auth context, so the serializer exposes a short-lived signed URL instead.
nodes.norm_label: signed blob url download (not server redirect)

nodes.label: FiltersAggregator (disjunctive counts)
nodes.author: Damian
nodes.rationale: Selecting a value under one option type was showing wrong sibling counts because counts were computed against the already-filtered set; fix groups selected values by option type server-side and computes disjunctive counts per type.

nodes.label: Meilisearch N+1 multi-search for facets
nodes.author: Damian
nodes.rationale: 1 hit query + 1 facet query per active option type, batched via /multi-search, mirrors Algolia's disjunctive faceting pattern.

nodes.label: RichText translation storage asymmetry
nodes.author: Damian
nodes.rationale: Default-locale RichText stays in ActionText; translated values are stored as HTML in the translation table, temporary until 6.0 ActionText removal makes it symmetric.

nodes.label: Text-only metafield translatability
nodes.author: Damian
nodes.rationale: Only ShortText/LongText/RichText are translatable, matching Shopify/Saleor/Vendure industry consensus; Number/Boolean/Json are not translatable.

nodes.label: read_/write_ per-resource scope vocabulary
nodes.author: Damian
nodes.rationale: CanCanCan resolves abilities from a current_user, a poor fit for API keys representing integrations not users; mirrors Shopify access scopes and Saleor app permissions.

nodes.label: ScopedAuthorization concern
nodes.author: Damian
nodes.rationale: scoped_resource declared per controller (not auto-derived) so nested controllers can map to a different scope than their parent.

nodes.label: Spree::Api::V3::BulkOperations concern
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: Resolved bulk envelope question: per-action bulk routes with { ids: [...] } bodies, not a single generic /bulk endpoint.

nodes.label: 6.0 endpoint rename/removal table
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: Tracks taxonomies/shipping_methods/zones/return_authorizations/prototypes/metafield_definitions renames so contributors don't re-implement removed endpoints.

nodes.label: Admin::ResourceController hierarchy
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: All admin controllers inherit from Admin::ResourceController for default CRUD; admin serializers extend Store serializers so public fields propagate automatically.

nodes.label: No <SpreeField>/<SpreeForm> wrapper decision
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: A Rails-FormBuilder-equivalent wrapper was tried and reverted; the Rails analogy was misleading because RHF, Zod, the SDK, and react-i18next are decoupled layers in a React SPA, and bridging them implicitly made forms harder to debug than the verbose raw RHF original.

nodes.label: cus_ → cust_ prefix transition
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: 5.5 keeps cus_ (existing has_prefix_id :cus); 6.0 renames Spree::User to Spree::Customer and prefix to cust_, both must resolve through the SDK type during transition.

nodes.label: Addresses as sub-resource (Medusa pattern)
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: POST /customers/:id/addresses with is_default_billing/is_default_shipping flags on the address rather than nested attributes or Shopify's single default_address — needed for B2B differing bill/ship defaults.

nodes.label: dashboard / dashboard-core / dashboard-ui package split
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: Matches the 3/3 industry pattern (Medusa, Vendure, Saleor) of UI-primitives + extension-SDK + app; goes further by making dashboard-ui carry both primitives and headless composed components, unlike any competitor.

nodes.label: Slot registry / <Slot> API
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the Rails admin's render_admin_partials slot mechanism so plugin authors carry their mental model across; named slots chosen over render-prop overrides because they're append-only and composable.

nodes.label: Table registry (defineTable)
nodes.author: damian
nodes.rationale: Declarative resource list page definition mirroring Rails admin's Spree.admin.tables DSL.

nodes.label: CLI Credential Resolution Layers
nodes.rationale: Host and key resolve together per source so a saved or minted key is never silently re-pointed at a different host; only --base-url or SPREE_BASE_URL paired with SPREE_API_KEY re-points deliberately.

nodes.label: Spree Extension Points
nodes.rationale: Events and Dependencies are preferred over Decorators for most customizations because they are easier to maintain and won't break during upgrades.

nodes.label: Server-driven CanCanCan permissions in the SPA
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v3/admin/me returns serialized CanCanCan abilities so the SPA can mirror permission checks for UX, while the server still enforces authorize! on every request as the real gate.
nodes.norm_label: server-driven cancancan permissions in the spa

nodes.label: Dashboard JWT + cookie refresh auth
nodes.rationale: Access token kept only in React state (no localStorage/sessionStorage) with the refresh token in an HttpOnly signed cookie, so an XSS payload cannot exfiltrate long-lived credentials; CSRF defense comes from SameSite + AllowedOrigin rather than a double-submit token.

nodes.label: Subclass + Dependencies Swap Pattern
nodes.rationale: Core serializers are customized by subclassing and registering the subclass via Spree::Api::Dependencies rather than decorating, because it is explicit, testable, and lets other extensions further subclass the result.

nodes.label: Expand Query Parameter System
nodes.rationale: Associations like brand are excluded from responses by default and only included when the client requests ?expand=brand, keeping default payloads lean while allowing opt-in nested data.

nodes.label: Model "Owned Once" Generator Rule
nodes.rationale: Once a model exists, api_resource generator skips model/migration creation and only adds API surface files, so domain code is owned once by the developer and never silently overwritten by later generator runs.

nodes.label: Async-by-Default Subscribers
nodes.rationale: Subscribers run as ActiveJobs on the events queue by default so a slow external API (e.g. an OMS) never blocks checkout; synchronous execution is opt-in via async: false.

nodes.label: Decorator Pattern (Module#prepend)
nodes.rationale: Decorators (Ruby modules prepended into core classes) let developers add associations/validations/scopes to Spree::Product etc. without editing core source, so upgrades don't clobber customizations and the origin of changes stays traceable.

nodes.label: Events Preferred Over Decorator Callbacks
nodes.rationale: For side effects (syncing to external services, notifications), Events subscribers are recommended over decorator-added callbacks because they are easier to test and don't break during Spree upgrades.

nodes.label: Removal of spree_auth_devise in Favor of Direct Devise Integration
nodes.norm_label: removal of spree_auth_devise in favor of direct devise integration

nodes.label: Market Resolution from Country Header
nodes.rationale: X-Spree-Country resolves the customer's market, which then supplies default locale and currency unless explicitly overridden — allows per-region pricing, languages, and availability.

nodes.label: Vulnerability Disclosure Process
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities must be reported privately via email rather than public GitHub issues/PRs, to avoid exposing exploits before a fix ships across all supported versions; disclosure follows acknowledge (48h) -> confirm/assign severity -> fix+test -> release+advisory -> credit reporter.

nodes.label: Shopify to Spree Customer Column Mapping
nodes.norm_label: shopify to spree customer column mapping

nodes.label: Shopify to Spree Product Column Mapping
nodes.norm_label: shopify to spree product column mapping

nodes.label: Admin Role
nodes.rationale: Role-based access control is not yet fully implemented in the admin UI; role names can be created but only take effect via code-configured permissions.

nodes.label: Canonical Decimal String Money Format
nodes.rationale: Monetary values are represented as period-decimal strings (not JSON numbers) to preserve decimal precision and avoid floating-point rounding issues; format is locale-independent, with localized formatting handled client-side before sending.

nodes.label: Default Marketplace Commission Rate
nodes.rationale: Sets the baseline commission rate applied to all newly invited vendors; only affects future invitations so existing vendor relationships are not silently altered.

nodes.label: Preferred Vendor Payouts Schedule Interval
nodes.rationale: Marketplace-wide default payout cadence; vendors can opt to follow it or set their own schedule, balancing operational simplicity with vendor flexibility.

nodes.label: Product-Specific Commission Rate
nodes.rationale: Most specific override level, used when a vendor's catalog has items with different margins; wins over both vendor-specific and marketplace default rates.

nodes.label: Suborder
nodes.rationale: After a single unified checkout, Spree splits the customer's order into one suborder per vendor so each can fulfil independently without cross-vendor coordination.

nodes.label: Vendor Status Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Tracks a vendor relationship through Invited, Onboarding, Ready for Review, Approved, Rejected, or Suspended states.

nodes.label: Manual/CSV Onboarding Flow
nodes.rationale: Catch-all onboarding path for vendors without Shopify/WooCommerce, requiring the spree_multi_vendor Enterprise gem and manual setup of shipping, billing, returns, and Stripe.

nodes.label: Shopify Custom App (Custom Distribution)
nodes.rationale: Spree connects each vendor's Shopify store via a dedicated Custom App distributed through Custom Distribution rather than the Shopify Sales Channel App pattern, since each vendor is a specific known store.

nodes.label: WooCommerce Onboarding Flow
nodes.rationale: Shipping methods sync automatically from WooCommerce but rates must be set manually, unlike Shopify where both sync.

nodes.label: Vendor-Specific Payout Schedule
nodes.rationale: Payouts run through Stripe Connect; a vendor can override the marketplace default interval or keep following it, with the vendor-specific choice always taking precedence when set.

nodes.label: Cart as Explicit REST Resource
nodes.rationale: Collapsing checkout into the cart resource (stable prefixed ID, nested fulfillments/payments) removes step transitions and implicit current-cart state, enabling Shopify-style one-page checkout and multiple saved carts per customer/organization.

nodes.label: Checkout State Machine (v2)
nodes.rationale: The five-step checkout state machine made cart/checkout calls easy to write but hard to reason about, since the same payload could land in different states depending on the current step; v3 removes it entirely.

nodes.label: Flat JSON Response Format
nodes.rationale: Returns resources directly with associations inlined via expand, avoiding the noisy wire format and two-step deserialization JSON:API required.

nodes.label: JSON:API Format
nodes.rationale: JSON:API's sparse fieldsets and normalized payloads were real strengths, but most storefront clients flattened the response anyway, causing a noisy wire format and two-step deserialization; v3 drops it for flat JSON with expand-based association inlining.

nodes.label: Payment Sessions API
nodes.rationale: Unifies per-gateway endpoints (Stripe, Adyen, PayPal) behind a generic API so Spree dispatches to the right provider based on payment_method_id, shortening integration time and avoiding frontend code changes per gateway.

nodes.label: Community Edition vs Enterprise Edition
nodes.rationale: Community Edition trades enterprise support/features for full DIY freedom; Enterprise Edition trades cost for saved time, more security, and more integrations - letting adopters choose based on control vs. convenience tradeoffs.

nodes.label: Franchise/Reseller Network
nodes.rationale: Centralizes catalog, payments, and fulfillment under a parent business so franchisees/resellers gain branded storefronts without operational complexity, trading tenant autonomy for brand consistency.

nodes.label: Multi-Brand Enterprise
nodes.rationale: Unlike marketplaces or SaaS tenants, brand stores are internally owned, so there's no need for self-service onboarding or billing - the model optimizes for operational efficiency and consistency across owned brands.

nodes.label: PCI Compliance
nodes.rationale: Spree never stores or processes raw card data itself, delegating to PCI-DSS compliant processors like Stripe/Adyen and retaining only encrypted tokens and non-sensitive metadata, minimizing its own compliance surface.

nodes.label: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Alignment
nodes.rationale: Spree is self-hosted so it cannot itself be certified under SOC 2/ISO 27001, but its security controls are modeled on equivalent best-practice frameworks so enterprise customers can align their own certification efforts.

nodes.label: Super Admin Role
nodes.rationale: Sits at the control end of the multi-tenant 'control spectrum,' from full centralization to full tenant autonomy, so a single platform can support both tightly managed and hands-off business models.

nodes.label: Approval Workflows & ERP Integrations
nodes.rationale: Reserved for Enterprise Edition because role-based approval chains and pre-built ERP/procurement connectors serve complex back-office integration needs beyond the open-source core.

nodes.label: B2B Catalogs
nodes.rationale: Roadmap feature (Spree 6.0) for curated per-segment product assortments, so different buyer groups see different subsets of the catalog without maintaining separate stores.

nodes.label: Buyer Organizations
nodes.rationale: Roadmap feature (Spree 6.0) allowing multiple buyers to operate under one company account with shared order history, addressing the need for role-based buyer structures in B2B commerce.

nodes.label: Cookie-backed admin authentication
nodes.rationale: Refresh token moved from JSON body to an HttpOnly signed cookie scoped to /api/v3/admin/auth to eliminate the most attractive XSS target on the admin SPA; CSRF is covered by SameSite + the AllowedOrigin allowlist instead of a separate CSRF token.

nodes.label: Market
nodes.rationale: Defines distinct shopping experiences (currency, language, tax) per region/segment, avoiding product duplication by acting as a Price List rule condition instead.

nodes.label: Order Routing Strategy
nodes.rationale: Determines which stock location fulfils an order across multiple warehouses; Rules (ordered) strategy layers Preferred location, Minimize stock locations, and Default location rules in priority order.

nodes.label: Sales Channel
nodes.rationale: Lets a single Spree instance run multiple distinct storefronts/selling contexts (POS, wholesale, mobile) each with its own catalog and order attribution, tagging orders automatically for filtering/routing.

nodes.label: Shipping Category
nodes.rationale: Groups products by delivery needs (e.g., Digital skips shipping step, Heavy restricts allowed methods) so different shipping methods can target different product types.

nodes.label: Tax Rate
nodes.rationale: Relies on the Zones feature to determine geographic applicability, tying tax logic to shipping address regions.

nodes.label: Zone
nodes.rationale: Groups geographic areas (country- or state-based) so tax, shipping, and market settings can be tailored to specific regions.

nodes.label: Importmap-rails
nodes.rationale: Used to manage JS dependencies without Node.js, npm, or Yarn; vendor libraries are pinned to vendor/javascript instead of node_modules.

nodes.label: Customization recommendation ordering (least to most invasive)
nodes.norm_label: customization recommendation ordering (least to most invasive)

nodes.label: Publishable API Key (pk_xxx)
nodes.rationale: Introduced because Storefront API v2 had no API key concept, so v3 requires one on every request to identify the target store and enable multi-store on a single domain, per-key rate limits, scopes and audit trails.

nodes.label: SDK Automatic Retry with Exponential Backoff
nodes.rationale: Respects Retry-After header and retries 429s (non-GET) and 500/502/503/504 (GET/HEAD) to smooth over transient rate limiting without requiring client-side retry logic.
nodes.norm_label: sdk automatic retry with exponential backoff

nodes.label: Automatic Link Label Resolution
nodes.rationale: When a link's linkable is set, the label is auto-populated from linkable.title, then display_name, then name, so store staff don't have to manually type labels for internal links.

nodes.label: Metafield Definition
nodes.rationale: Allows attaching custom structured data to store objects without code changes or database modification, reducing reliance on developer deployments.

nodes.label: @spree/dashboard-ui
nodes.rationale: Headless design-system rule: components accept data only via props and never import providers or hooks, making them pluggable into any React app.

nodes.label: Store API naming standardization vs industry conventions
nodes.rationale: Aligned Address/Cart/Order/OptionType/CreditCard field names with Shopify, Medusa, Saleor, and Vendure conventions (first_name/last_name, customer_note, label, brand/last4, etc.) so storefront integrators reuse existing mental models.
nodes.norm_label: store api naming standardization vs industry conventions

nodes.label: Customer Group
nodes.rationale: Groups are just lists on their own; value comes from pairing them with Price Lists and Promotion rules so retail and trade customers can shop the same storefront with personalized pricing, avoiding duplicate stores or logins.

nodes.label: Store Credit
nodes.rationale: Tied to a specific customer and non-transferable, unlike gift cards; can also serve as a primary B2B payment method for customers operating on prepaid balances or agreed credit thresholds.

nodes.label: Monetary Values as Strings
nodes.rationale: Monetary values are returned as strings rather than numbers to preserve decimal precision and avoid floating-point rounding issues common with JSON numbers.

nodes.label: Secret API Key Scopes (read_*/write_*)
nodes.rationale: write_<resource> implies read_<resource>; webhooks and api_keys scopes kept separate from settings because they are security-sensitive (webhook endpoints can exfiltrate data to arbitrary URLs; api_keys controls credential minting and scopes can never be amplified through the API).

nodes.label: Secret API Key (sk_xxx)
nodes.rationale: Server-to-server only; grants full administrative access and must never be embedded in client-side code.

nodes.label: Optimistic Locking (state_lock_version)
nodes.rationale: Every state-changing order operation increments state_lock_version; concurrent writes fail the second caller with cart_already_updated (409) so it can refetch and retry, protecting against race conditions under concurrency.

nodes.label: Importmaps Dependency Management
nodes.rationale: Rails Storefront uses Importmaps instead of Node.js/npm/Yarn to manage JS dependencies, avoiding a Node build toolchain; jsbundling-rails is offered as an alternative for teams wanting a different package manager.

nodes.label: Admin money field typing (non-nullable)
nodes.rationale: Admin money fields remain non-nullable because storefront price gating never applies to the Admin API.

nodes.label: Nullable money fields under gated storefront
nodes.rationale: On a prices_hidden channel the Store API nulls out every monetary amount, including on nested records inside a cart/order, so anonymous visitors cannot recover hidden prices through a side channel.
nodes.norm_label: nullable money fields under gated storefront

nodes.label: Store storefront access gating
nodes.rationale: Store.preferred_storefront_access (public/prices_hidden/login_required) and preferred_guest_checkout let channels inherit a store-level fallback posture instead of each channel configuring its own.

nodes.label: tables registry (list-view column extensions)
nodes.rationale: Built-in tables register lazily via side-effect imports in route files, so the registry queues mutations from plugins that load first and replays them once the table registers — mutations targeting a table that never registers stay pending by design.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key Header
nodes.rationale: Caches the response for 24 hours so retries of the same request (same key + params) safely return the original response instead of re-executing the mutation; a key reused with different parameters is rejected with a 422 to prevent misuse.

nodes.label: Fork-and-Track-Upstream Strategy
nodes.rationale: Forking the storefront starter repo (rather than copying it) lets teams customize freely while still pulling upstream updates via a tracked remote.

nodes.label: Next.js Recommended Over Rails Storefront
nodes.rationale: Spree recommends the Next.js Storefront for new projects over the Rails Storefront because it offers better performance and a more modern developer experience.

nodes.label: Webhook Signature Verification
nodes.rationale: Webhook payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over "timestamp.body" so receivers can verify authenticity before trusting the payload; failed deliveries are recorded (not auto-retried) and endpoints auto-disable after 15 consecutive failures.

nodes.label: Lazy Loading Sections Pattern
nodes.rationale: Sections that load external data (products, taxons) implement lazy? and lazy_path so they render asynchronously after initial page load, improving page performance.

nodes.label: Metadata vs Metafields Distinction
nodes.rationale: Metadata is a schemaless, unvalidated developer escape hatch (write-only in Store API, readable in Admin API) for integration/tracking data — 'metadata for machines'. Metafields are typed, schema-defined, merchant-facing structured attributes validated against a MetafieldDefinition — 'metafields for humans'. Both are permanent, complementary systems, not a migration path.

nodes.label: Spree Headless Platform Principle
nodes.rationale: Spree is a headless platform; legacy tightly-coupled frontend gems (spree_storefront, spree_frontend) are deprecated in favor of a Next.js storefront or custom storefront built on Store API v3.

nodes.label: Payment Tokenization
nodes.rationale: Spree never transmits or stores raw credit card numbers; instead payment processor tokens (from gateway frontend SDKs like Stripe.js, Adyen Drop-in) are used, so sensitive data never touches the Spree server, avoiding most PCI scope.

nodes.label: Server-First Architecture Pattern
nodes.rationale: All Spree API calls happen server-side via Server Actions so the Spree API key and auth tokens never reach the browser; httpOnly cookies store tokens, keeping JWTs inaccessible to client-side JS.

nodes.label: Server-Side Only Env Vars Rationale
nodes.rationale: SPREE_API_URL and SPREE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY need no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix because all API calls happen in Server Actions, keeping them out of client bundles.
